main_text.l: Tum Gaius, qui praesul erat Romanus, in altis Delituit cryptis. Tunc Marcellinus et ipse, Romulidum pastor, uictus formidine Christum Prodidit, et plena Marti libauit acerra.

Marcellinus Romanus, decima persecutione post Neronem, cum grauissime sub Diocletiano et Maximiano, a tortoribus urgeretur, poenarum timore correptus, thuris granum idolis adoleuit. Erant tuno sacrae scripturae (inquit noster Gildas) quaecunque inueniri poterant, in publicis plateis exustae: et electi sacerdotes gregis Domini, cum innocentissimis ouibus trucidati. Sed in se statim reuersus Marcellinus, agnito errore, Diocletianum ipsum redarguit, et ad necem pro Christi veritate seipsum lubens obtulit, anno Domini 303. fortissimeque pugnans uicit, accepta martyrij laurea. His astipulatur praedictus Mantuanus, in suo Bla-fio[?]:

At scelus id mox erubuit, sensuque recepto, Incepit damnare Deos, extollere Christum: Nec mors horribilis uisa est, sed sponte cucurrit In medios hostes, iugulumque tetendit ad ensem. Fortior in pugnam post signa amissa reuersus Victor, et ornatus uiridi discessit oliua.

page.notes: Small marks "cc" and "/." in the right margin beside the lines "Maximiano" and "exustae", possibly reference or printer's marks; not transcribed as text. Long s is printed as f in the scan and is given as plain s. "uiclus" in the verse may be printed "uictus"; the word was read as "uictus" with the printed letters uncertain. The hyphenated word "Bla-fio" is read with doubt, as the printer's "Blasphemio". The catchword is read as "Mart", partly unclear.
